plan.question: For short, under-fitting CIFAR-scale training runs (~8-10 epochs, small whitened CNN like airbench96, batch ~1024), what does the literature say about progressive resizing: training the early fraction of steps at reduced resolution (e.g. 24 px, then 32 px)? Specifically: (1) how much final accuracy does it cost or gain at a fixed step count, and how does that depend on the low-res step fraction, the low resolution, and the resize method (bilinear vs. random-resized crop vs. antialias)? (2) What decides it: the train/test resolution discrepancy (FixRes), the scale shift for BN statistics and first-layer filters (here a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening conv computed at 32 px), or coupling of regularization strength to resolution (as in progressive learning / EfficientNetV2)? (3) Do measured wall-clock savings match the ~44% FLOP cut per low-res step for small GPU-bound convnets, or do fixed per-step overheads erase them? Note: E004 is the 8.5-epoch, no-cutout, label-smoothing-0.1 recipe, not a 10-epoch one; the experiment should start from E004 as it actually ran.
queries: progressive resizing training speedup image classification
progressive learning adaptive regularization image size EfficientNetV2
budgeted training low resolution early epochs CIFAR
mixed resolution training convolutional networks fast training
rubric: Trains with a resolution schedule (low-res early, full-res late, or a mix of resolutions) and reports final accuracy against a fixed-resolution baseline at matched steps or matched wall-clock time.
Uses a short or compute-budgeted schedule, or small images (CIFAR, downsampled ImageNet, ImageNet at low res), so the results carry over to an ~8-10 epoch under-fitting regime.
Explains or ablates the mechanism: the low-res fraction, train/test resolution mismatch, BN statistic or receptive-field shift, the interpolation method, or regularization scaled with image size.
Reports measured wall-clock or throughput savings, not only FLOPs.
exclude: Methods that need pretrained weights, transfer learning, or external or extra data (forbidden by RULES.md)
Test-time augmentation or test-set-dependent resolution tuning, e.g. FixRes fine-tuning on test-time statistics or multi-resolution test ensembles
Super-resolution or image-generation papers on resolution that do not deal with classifier training efficiency
Large-scale distributed or ViT-only token-dropping/patch-resizing work that has no convnet or small-image result
Fine-tuning a classifier at higher resolution after training is finished
